pageCache.text:
News Blog
Science Club Fun
On Thursday Science club used cyanotype paper, and acetate to create images by blocking out UV rays from the sun.
Cyanotype is one of the earliest photographic techniques, developed in 1842 by Sir John Herschel initially as a method to reproduce notes and diagrams.
The boys worked hard on their original images on acetate, these were then left to develop using sunlight and these are the end results.

pageCache.pageTitle: KS3 Science Club trip to Science Live, London - News Blog - Dover Grammar School for Boys
pageCache.text:
News Blog
KS3 Science Club trip to Science Live, London
We attended a range exciting lectures by some prominent people. Students particularly enjoyed Dr Maggie Aderin-Pocock pose and answer the questions; Are we made of star dust? And is there other life in Space?
Professor Robert Winston spoke about IVF and developments in this field and took questions from the audience.
Dr Anna Ploszajski gave an engaging talk and demonstration about the importance of materials and their properties for her channel swim. From a chocolate Swiss roll that is buoyant, high energy and waterproof to the design of her swim costume. She also linked swimwear used in the Olympics to biomimicry and why ‘shark suits’ are now banned due to the unfair advantage that they gave!

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher's Welcome - Dover Grammar School for Boys
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
A very warm welcome to Dover Grammar School for Boys. If this is your first visit to our website, I hope that you will find much here to give you a picture of who we are as a school and what we represent.
I am extremely proud to be Headteacher of a school which is very much at the heart of the local community, serving students and their parents and helping our learners to grow and develop into the best versions of themselves.
Our school is a learning community with a vision and ethos that has been developed and committed to by all its members – students, staff, parents and governors. Guided by our school motto - "Fiat Lux" or "Let there be light" - we value intellectual curiosity, engagement, empathy, aspirational thinking and a keen desire to learn and improve. However, above all we want our students to be happy and engaged during their time with us. Indeed, in my experience, happy students are always successful students.
We look to stimulate and challenge the minds of our students through both their academic studies and the wealth of enriching extra-curricular experiences in which they participate. We are developing a technology-rich learning environment that ensures our students gain the skills to cope with the ever changing needs of employers as well as learning to interact safely and responsibly with the online community. We ensure that our curriculum is constantly evolving to reflect the society that we live in and to provide students with the opportunity to engage with our wider local community through work placements, volunteering and collaborative projects. It is our aim for every member of the DGSB community to be proud of his or her school and the part that each individual plays in adding to its long and impressive history.

pageCache.text:
News Blog
History Trip to Washington DC
Over three memorable days at the start of April, 26 Year 9 and 10 students enjoyed a history trip to Washington DC. The visit began on Capitol Hill, where we explored the heart of American democracy. Whilst here, a protest outside the Supreme Court was witnessed as Donald Trump became the first ever President to sit in on a hearing. This was followed by a true American cultural experience in the evening by attending an NBA fixture between the Washington Wizards and the Philadelphia 76ers.
On day two we saw the White House, visited several of Washington’s powerful memorials, including the Lincoln Memorial, the World War II Memorial and the Vietnam Veterans Memorial. These sites encouraged reflection on sacrifice and freedom. A particularly moving experience was our visit to Arlington Cemetery, where students observed the Changing of the Guard at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, whilst also observing moments of reflection at the grave of John F Kennedy and the Lockerbie bombing memorial.
On the final day of the trip students explored several museums, including exhibits on American history, science, politics and culture. These hands‑on experiences deepened understanding and inspired curiosity, making the trip an engaging and educational success for all involved. The students had a jam packed fascinating tour of the nation’s capitol, and will have made memories to last a lifetime.

pageCache.text:
Personal Development and Rewards
Enrichment
All students in Year 12 and 13 will participate in one session of enrichment per week. The sessions will run on a rotation basis and will provide opportunities for the following;
- Food tech (Essential cookery skills for life)
- Financial Literacy (Tax, Budgeting, Mortgages and Loans)
- Creative (Art, Music Workshops, Small Media Productions)
- RSE (Following the DGSB PSHE spiral curriculum)
- DGSB Sixth Form Newspaper
Where possible, external speakers, artists and an array of experts in a range of different fields will support the running of the sessions. Once a term, students will also be given a chance to plan and run their own enrichment sessions.
Sport
Whilst students will no longer take core PE lessons, we believe that it is important that they access some sport throughout their time in Sixth Form. In the 2025-26 academic year, we introduced the very popular Sixth Form 5-aside league. We are delighted too that in 2025-26 we have been able to field our first ever all girls Sixth Form netball team. Finally, students wishing to represent the school will have the chance to play for either the First XI or Second XI football team.
Fiat Lux, Rewards and Driving Lessons
Recognising Student Achievement
Students are encouraged to work hard, and their efforts are acknowledged by both teachers and the KS5 Team through ‘Shout Outs’ in weekly assemblies.
As an incentive to reach their potential, students will be offered the chance to claim back money that has been spent on driving lessons. Students performing at the very top of the year group will be eligible for varying amounts of funding towards driving lessons.
In Year 12 we place a significant emphasis on the importance of participation in the wider school community. Students are expected to use their free periods in order to mentor younger students both academically and pastorally as well as running clubs and more. Students can access the ‘Fiat Lux’ timetable and choose an activity to engage with, receiving tokens for their efforts which can be exchanged for a range of different awards. These can include;
- Vouchers for local restaurants and eateries (including the sixth form central cafe)
- Bookable early afternoon finishes (where they might otherwise have a free period of study period)
- Travel mugs and stationery
Senior Fiat Lux Scholars and wider school responsibilities
We endeavour to encourage student leadership and community engagement. Our Senior Fiat Lux Scholars meet weekly in order to share ideas that will positively develop the Sixth Form and take leadership roles in making these changes happen as well as take on the responsibility to support during school events and help run our regular charity events.
Trips and Events
Each year, as part of an initial team building activity we take all Year 12 students to ‘Boonies’, the assault course at Betteshanger Country Park. Students will also be able to participate in an end of year rewards trip to a bowling alley and water park. In Year 13 we hold a ‘Leavers Awards Ceremony’ to reflect and celebrate their time with us.

DGSB IT Systems for Parents and Students
Please see below for information on the main IT programmes students and parents need, including what they are, what they are for and how to access them.
ParentMail
This free app helps you to be kept in touch with DGSB news and events. The app gives you direct access to your child’s attendance, absence records, school reports and so much more. It is the place to make payments for items such as school lunches.
For first time registration you will have received a registration email containing a link to the website. Registering requires you to enter the date of birth of your child and to complete the registration steps. The app is available for both Apple and Android devices. To set it up simply: 1) Go to your App Store 2) Search for ParentMail 3) Download the free IRIS ParentMail app. 4) Once downloaded, search for Dover Grammar School for Boys and follow the identification steps. Afterwards logging in is straightforward using either the app or website.
Class Charts
This is a new and highly recommended service used by over one-thousand UK schools to help parents and students see progress and behaviour in lessons. Data from Class Charts builds towards milestone achievements and rewards for students.
There are two main ways that both parents and students can use Class Charts.
– Easiest and most convenient way is an App on either Android or Apple phones
– The second method is to login through www.classcharts.com
Parents of new students receive their individual log in details (via email/taken home by their son/posted on ParentMail) to allow them to log in.
Office 365
Office 365 offers online versions of Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), is a place to store files online (using OneDrive) and subjects place their lessons and resources in class Teams for ease of access by students at any time through an internet connection. Office 365 works on tablets, smartphones, laptops and PCs. It works on any operating system that supports chromium web browsers (eg. Windows, MacOS, Linux).
Student user accounts and password reset are done in the first few Computing lessons. Student usernames for getting on the network in school have the format: Initial of first name, surname, 22. For example a Year 7 student called John Smith would have the username: jsmith22. Office 365 accounts are accessed using an email address that comprise of the username followed by ‘@dgsb.co.uk’. For example: jsmith22@dgsb.co.uk. Passwords are reset by students on first login. Students who forget their password should go directly to the IT Office on the first floor, located near the central stairwell. IT Services can be contacted on: IT@dgsb.co.uk When signing in to Office 365 at home the best way is to open Google Chrome web browser and enter: office.com as a search in the address bar of the browser. On the Microsoft web page that opens click on the Sign In button.

DGSB IT Systems for Parents and Students
Please see below for information on the main IT programmes students and parents need, including what they are, what they are for and how to access them.
ParentMail
This free app helps you to be kept in touch with DGSB news and events. The app gives you direct access to your child’s attendance, absence records, school reports and so much more. It is the place to make payments for items such as school lunches.
For first time registration you will have received a registration email containing a link to the website. Registering requires you to enter the date of birth of your child and to complete the registration steps. The app is available for both Apple and Android devices. To set it up simply: 1) Go to your App Store 2) Search for ParentMail 3) Download the free IRIS ParentMail app. 4) Once downloaded, search for Dover Grammar School for Boys and follow the identification steps. Afterwards logging in is straightforward using either the app or website.
Class Charts
This is a new and highly recommended service used by over one-thousand UK schools to help parents and students see progress and behaviour in lessons. Data from Class Charts builds towards milestone achievements and rewards for students.
There are two main ways that both parents and students can use Class Charts.
– Easiest and most convenient way is an App on either Android or Apple phones
– The second method is to login through www.classcharts.com
Parents of new students receive their individual log in details (via email/taken home by their son/posted on ParentMail) to allow them to log in.
Office 365
Office 365 offers online versions of Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), is a place to store files online (using OneDrive) and subjects place their lessons and resources in class Teams for ease of access by students at any time through an internet connection. Office 365 works on tablets, smartphones, laptops and PCs. It works on any operating system that supports chromium web browsers (eg. Windows, MacOS, Linux).
Student user accounts and password reset are done in the first few Computing lessons. Student usernames for getting on the network in school have the format: Initial of first name, surname, 22. For example a Year 7 student called John Smith would have the username: jsmith22. Office 365 accounts are accessed using an email address that comprise of the username followed by ‘@dgsb.co.uk’. For example: jsmith22@dgsb.co.uk. Passwords are reset by students on first login. Students who forget their password should go directly to the IT Office on the first floor, located near the central stairwell. IT Services can be contacted on: IT@dgsb.co.uk When signing in to Office 365 at home the best way is to open Google Chrome web browser and enter: office.com as a search in the address bar of the browser. On the Microsoft web page that opens click on the Sign In button.

Reporting Absence
In order to ensure that the Attendance Officer receives absence information at the earliest opportunity and through the correct communication channel, please note of the information below.
Short term and unplanned absence
Parents should contact the school by 9am on the day of the absence via the Class Charts app.
This messaging service is the method all parents/carers must use to report short term and unplanned absence that is typically due to last-minute illness, injury, and emergency appointments etc.
Long term absence
The school has a dedicated email address attendance@dgsb.co.uk where long term/multiple appointments, religious holidays and holiday requests, family related absence, and planned extended absences should be sent to inform staff and obtain the relevant authorisation if required. The information will then be forwarded to the appropriate Key Stage team(s) meaning only one email needs to be sent which prevents repetition of information.
All requests for absence in advance will need to be submitted via the above email address.
As a last resort, absence can be reported using the main school number 01304 206117 selecting Option 1. This route should only be used if you are unable to access the Class Charts app or the email address given above.
In addition, if you are emailing the Key stage team and is attendance related, please can you ensure the Attendance Officer is also included. The Key Stage teams are extremely busy and do not always have time to read and forward to the Attendance Officer, in time before the absence alerts are sent. Thank you for your continued support with this important process.

pageCache.text:
Careers in the Sixth Form
Careers education continues in the DGSB Sixth Form, with students being supported in whichever steps they wish to take next after they have completed their A-Levels.
All students in year 12 have a careers interview which takes place with an independent career’s advisor. This allows all students to ask any questions they have about a career area they are interested in as well as getting support in which routes they could take towards gaining the required qualifications. The interviews are all one-to-one, ensuring that students receive bespoke guidance that will best support them in their future decisions.
Careers activities take place during timetabled Enrichment sessions, with students in Year 12 taking part in supportive career sessions focused on the key employability skills, such as interview types and techniques and writing perfect cover letters and CVs. These are expanded in Year 13 to support students in completing university applications and writing personal statements to promote themselves, to either a potential university or employer.
In March we have our DGSB Futures Week, which consists of visits from future education providers, experts from the world of industry sharing their experiences, workshops for students focusing on both employability skills and the relevant next steps they will be taking, and trips to workplaces and universities to help all students make an informed decision as to which career path they would like to follow.
All students in the DGSB Sixth Form are supported by their form tutors in whichever path they would like to follow, from the completion of application forms to guidance in writing application statements.
